resolutions.researcher_notes: Status 'operating' is inferred, not literal. ecns.cn (Aug 13 2024) reports the offshore GOSP platform for the Marjan field was delivered/completed after a 34-month build and will let the field ramp up output, transporting 7.4 bcm of gas annually + crude for Aramco -> operating by context. offshore-technology describes the same GOSP-4 expansion as commissioned (it says 2025). Minor date discrepancy: ecns implies 2024 delivery, offshore-technology says commissioned 2025 (see Start note). Both independent (Chinese state media vs UK trade site), both confirm the plant/pipelines reached completion, supporting 'operating'.

Fuel = Gas well supported. offshore-energy: Package 4 is EPCI of 'offshore gas facilities and pipelines' for the Marjan Increment. nsenergybusiness: GOSP-4 designed to handle ~750 Mscfd of gas with associated subsea gas infrastructure. Two independent trade sources.

PipelineType 'transmission' inferred from scope: offshore-energy describes 'subsea trunk lines and in-field pipelines' (trunk lines = transmission); nsenergybusiness describes subsea trunk/export pipelines carrying field production to shore. No source uses the literal word 'transmission', but trunk-line + field-to-shore role supports it. Two independent sources.

ConstructionYear 2019 = year Aramco awarded the Package 4 EPCI contract to McDermott (offshore-energy dated 2019-07-10; argaam Saudi-market report on the $4.5b Marjan package awards, 2019). Note: the same offshore-energy article puts actual fabrication at Q1 2020 through Q4 2022, so 2019 reflects award/EPCI kickoff rather than physical construction start; flagged but the 2019 stamp is supported by two independent sources.

StartYear1 2024 supported by 2024 completion/delivery of the Marjan GOSP offshore platform: ecns.cn (Aug 13 2024, platform delivered, field to ramp up output). china.aramco (Aramco's own release on completing fabrication of the platform in China, 2024) cited via Wayback because the live page timed out; Wayback snapshot verified OK/200 with 'Marjan' present. CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: offshore-technology says the expansion was commissioned 2025, so first gas/start could be 2024 (platform delivered) or 2025 (commissioning) - value 2024 is defensible but not unanimous.

Could not independently corroborate LengthKnown = 62.00 mi for the GAS pipeline. Independent sources give: offshore-energy/mcdermott = 'in excess of 330 mi (540 km)' of subsea trunk lines AND in-field pipelines combined (Package 4 aggregate, not a single gas line); nsenergybusiness/offshore-technology = 540 km trunk+in-field, 217 km fixed pipelines, plus a 70 km 36-in OIL export line. The 62 mi (~100 km) figure appears to trace to a 36-in subsea OIL trunk line, not a gas pipeline, and no independent source states 62 mi for a gas line. Possible oil/gas conflation - value left UNRESOLVED and flagged for review.

Location supported: nsenergybusiness locates the Marjan field expansion in the 'Arabian Gulf, Saudi Arabia'; offshore-technology locates GOSP-4 in the 'Arabian Gulf, off Saudi Arabia's eastern coast'. Matches StartState/Province 'Arabian Gulf', StartPrefecture/District 'Eastern Coast', country Saudi Arabia. Two independent sources.

Owner1 = Aramco (100%) well supported: offshore-energy and argaam both state Saudi Aramco is the project owner that awarded the Marjan Increment / GOSP-4 packages; McDermott is the EPCI contractor, not the owner. ecns.cn (2024) also names Aramco as owner of the delivered platform. Two+ independent sources agree; 100% Aramco ownership consistent with Aramco being the sole field operator/owner.
